TrueConeLoopPaper.exists_local_family_with_margin states Lemma C.1: same hypotheses (relaxed cone on the compact rectangle, admissible cone on a compact boundary set), a smooth period-one loop with a_L > 0, the mean condition (C.1) verbatim, a uniform cone margin, and agreement with the original shear near the boundary. Three encoding differences, all low: the margin is taken in (a, v_s−2, P_c−2, U−v_s) rather than in the gaps Ψ of (4.35); the single collar width δ∂ of (C.3) comes from the companion uniform_boundary_collar; and input smoothness is demanded on an open neighborhood of the closed rectangle. Each recovers routinely, the first through the already-formalized ConeAlgebra.true_cone_iff plus compactness. The Lean is also more general in the parameter space.

findings.summary: (C.2) asks for a uniform margin in the four cone gaps Ψ of (4.35); the Lean asserts a uniform margin in a different, equivalent quadruple (a, v_s−2, P_c−2, U(P_c,J_c)−v_s). Equal positivity sets, different numbers.
(C.3)'s single collar width δ∂ with dist(X,∂I) < δ∂ is not in the family theorem, which gives an unquantified open N ⊇ B; the width comes from a second declaration in the same file.
The Lean hypothesis is ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ on an open O ⊇ K, i.e. data smooth past η = ±1; the paper assumes smoothness only on the closed rectangle I × [−1,1], with one-sided η-derivatives.
